text: Muse Wonder is building the move

Slow 16mm push from 1.9m MLS at the door to 0.9m MCU tracks Maya centrally at the right slow pace for 9.2s while Theo moves from a sliver at the edge to a clear background figure without crossing the bunk. The background behind Maya ends on hanging jackets rather than the window, and the last 1.5m gets too tight with her over-filling foreground and Theo growing distracting at right plus a 0.9 to 1.0m drift-back from the clearance pinch. Shorten duration to 8.0s and pull the end key back to 1.2m to hold a clean MCU with 42cm clearance and keep the window behind her.

Headroom is cavernous and muddy overhead with zero look room, and Theo in blue is fully occluded behind Maya instead of holding the frame edge. She is backed by lockers rather than the window, so while 16mm is right the MLS at 1.9m is too tight for a doorway start; dolly back to the door for a wide establishing framing.

Headroom is tight to the top with Maya centered and no look room for her turn while Theo still hangs on the right edge at the end of the move. She is backed by cluttered shelves and hanging jackets, and the 16mm at 1.0m at this low height distorts the MCU and leaves only 40cm for handheld, so pull back to 1.6m on a 32mm at eye level and shift left to clear Theo.

The camera pushes from 1.9m to 0.9m onto the red foreground figure while the blue Maya at the window stays small in the background, the opposite of the requested push-in on Maya to MCU. Red starts near centre rather than tucked to the edge and swells to an over-tight MCU that blocks the view, leaving Maya still loose in MS against the lockers behind her. The 16mm handheld pace fits the 9.2s duration but the keys target the wrong subject, so reject and re-block the push to end on blue with red only as an edge sliver at the start.

Headroom is excessive and Maya has no look room toward the window, with cluttered lockers filling the background behind her instead of the window. The 16mm at 1.9m is too high and too wide to end on an undistorted medium close-up, so lower the camera to 1.4m and shift right to put Theo on the frame edge and the window behind Maya.

There is huge empty headroom above Maya with her face low in frame and no look room for her turn, while Theo in blue is still crowding the right edge at the end of the move. She is backed by hanging coveralls and yellow lockers instead of the window, and the 16mm at 0.9m is too wide and high for an intimate MCU, so reset to the door side of the bunk bed and restage the push to end on a 32mm MCU on the window.

Headroom is excessive above Maya with no look room toward the window she will turn to, while Theo sits too far inside frame instead of kissing the edge. Maya is backed by cluttered lockers rather than the window, though the 16mm height from the door suits the push-in without crossing the bunk; tilt down and pan right to place Theo on the right edge and the window behind Maya.

notes: A slow 9.15s handheld push-in at 16mm (operator 1.7m, shake 0.3, lens at 1.6m) from just inside the door at [1.55,-0.05] to [0.55,-0.20], tracking Maya's eyeline throughout as she holds at the window then turns from -90° to 80° in the last third, tightening cleanly from MLS at 1.92m through MS to a held MCU at 0.93m without overflowing frame; Theo is re-marked to [-2.69,0.21] on the west-north wall so he sits in the background edge of the wide opening and never stands between lens and Maya, and the whole path stays east of the bunk bed with no routed detour. The engine now reports feasible with zero problem/fail frames across all 221 frames (the earlier end key at [0.35,0.15] failed handheld clearance at 40cm vs the required 42cm, fixed by pulling back). Cost is minimal — one handheld operator, no track or rigging — but on the day watch the final metre for clearance beside the furniture, keep the walk slow and even so the MCU lands exactly as Maya completes her turn, and confirm Theo kisses the frame edge on the first frame rather than drifting centre.
